procedures.name: rsi
procedures.title: rapid sequence intubation
procedures.source: JTS CPG ID39, Airway Management in Trauma, 28 Jan 2026, Appendix I, Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI) and Intubation Pathway

steps.text: Confirm equipment availability and function: Suction, oxygen source, self-inflating bag and mask, oral & nasal airways, ETT with stylet and/or bougie, supraglottic airway, surgical airway kit, drugs, monitors, ventilator, laryngoscope- direct and video, CO2 detector.

Pre-Oxygenate (Denitrogenate) the lungs. Prolongs tolerance of apneic period. Goal is ≈ 3 minutes of tidal volume breathing at 90% FiO2. With standard reservoir facemask set flow rate of oxygen as high as possible. Recommend augmenting with nasal cannula at 15L/min oxygen in preparation for apneic oxygenation, leave in situ throughout procedure. Elevate head of bed if not contraindicated.
Maintain cervical spine stabilization
Remove front of cervical collar
Consider cricoid pressure simultaneous w/ medication administration

steps.signed: amended: unsigned drugs (etomidate) are not spoken
steps.text: Administer medications: Initiate RSI. ALWAYS SEDATE PRIOR TO PARALYZING. Sedative/hypnotic: Ketamine (First Line): 2 mg/kg IV/IO. Unstable patients require reduced dosage of induction agent.

steps.signed: amended: unsigned drugs (vecuronium) are not spoken
steps.text: Neuromuscular Blockade: Rocuronium: 1.2 mg/kg IV/IO or Succinylcholine: 1.5 mg/kg IV/IO
Perform laryngoscopic tracheal intubation. Following onset of neuromuscular blockade. Recommend gum elastic bougie as primary ETT stylet
If laryngoscopic view is poor: Apply external laryngeal manipulation technique(s). Consider alternative visualization method or Supraglottic airway device

Confirm tracheal intubation: Visualize tube passing between the vocal cords. Easy chest rise, equal axillary breath sounds/absence of gastric insufflation, CO2 Calorimeter, and "fog" in ETT. Wave form or digital capnography

steps.signed: amended: text as written, no dose computed
steps.text: Provide continuing care IAW JTS Anesthesia for Trauma Patients CPG
Have a dedicated pediatric airway cart, including Broselow tape or equivalent.
Pre-dose with atropine IV/IO (0.02mg/kg, minimum dose 0.1mg, maximum dose 0.5mg) in all <1 years old, those <5 who are receiving succinylcholine, and in all who receive a 2nd dose of succinylcholine

steps.signed: amended: unsigned drugs (etomidate) are not spoken
steps.text: Induction - Ketamine (first line) 2mg/kg IV/IO.
Neuromuscular blockade - Succinylcholine 1.5mg/kg IV/IO (2mg/kg <5 years old) or Rocuronium 1mg/kg IV/IO

procedures.name: failed airway
procedures.title: failed airway
procedures.source: JTS CPG ID39, Airway Management in Trauma, 28 Jan 2026, Appendix I, Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI) and Intubation Pathway

steps.text: Unable to Intubate: Can You Mask Ventilate? Improve position, video laryngoscope, gum elastic bougie change blade/operator.
More than ≈ 3 attempts at intubation may abolish your ability to mask ventilate due to edema caused by laryngoscopy.

steps.signed: as written (FA, the surgical airway line)
steps.text: YES → Surgical airway (Cricothyroidotomy or tracheostomy).
NO → Emergency pathway. Seconds matter. Supraglottic airway or Surgical cricothyroidotomy.
Avoid surgical airway in <12 years old - use needle cricothyroidotomy (12-14 gauge), tracheostomy preferred over surgical cricothyroidotomy
